Read it with lesson 4: the lesson explains the why, this5// file is the how.6//7// A program brings it in with two lines at the top, and still builds with8// plain rustc:9//10//   #[path = "../../includes/kayan.rs"]11//   mod kayan;12//13// What the program provides:14//15//   * an enum `ComponentId` with one member per component;16//   * its components, declared with component!(Name { field: Type, ... }),17//     which checks each is plain data, gives it the id of the ComponentId18//     member with the same name, and writes its reflect record;19//   * a w.register::<T>() for each component.20//21// Up to 64 components, because a signature is a u64.22//23// Not here, on purpose: threads, change tracking, chunked storage, relations.24// Each is worth a lesson of its own and none is needed to see the idea.25 26// Not every program calls every function here.27#![allow(dead_code)]28// `unsafe` is an error, except where an item allows it by name.29#![deny(unsafe_code)]30 31use std::alloc::Layout;32use std::collections::HashMap;33use std::fmt;34use std::num::NonZeroU32;35 36// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------37// Plain data, and what a tool can know about it38// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------39 40/// Plain old data: what lets a column hold a component as bytes, zero a row,41/// copy a row with a byte copy, and hand the bytes back as the type.42///43/// # Safety44///45/// The type is Copy, has no padding bytes, and every bit pattern is a valid46/// value of it. That is a promise the compiler cannot check by itself, so the47/// trait is unsafe; pod! makes the promise only after checking it at compile48/// time.49#[allow(unsafe_code)]50pub unsafe trait Pod: Copy + 'static {}51 52#[allow(unsafe_code)]53unsafe impl Pod for f32 {}54#[allow(unsafe_code)]55unsafe impl Pod for u32 {}56#[allow(unsafe_code)]57unsafe impl Pod for i32 {}58#[allow(unsafe_code)]59unsafe impl<const N: usize> Pod for [u8; N] {}60 61// A reflect record: a type's name, size and alignment, and what its bytes are.62// The compiler knows all of it; the macros below write it down.63pub struct Info {64    pub name: &'static str,65    pub layout: Layout,66    pub kind: Kind,67}68 69pub enum Kind {70    F32,71    U32,72    I32,73    // A [u8; N]: text, padded with zeros.74    Text,75    // An i32 that is one of these named values (pod_enum!).76    Enum(&'static [(&'static str, i32)]),77    // A struct, field by field (pod!).78    Struct(&'static [Field]),79}80 81// One field: where its bytes start in the struct, and the record of its type.82// `hidden` marks bookkeeping a tool need not show.83pub struct Field {84    pub name: &'static str,85    pub offset: usize,86    pub info: &'static Info,87    pub hidden: bool,88}89 90// Every type a component is made of has a record.91pub trait Reflect {92    const INFO: &'static Info;93}94 95impl Reflect for f32 {96    const INFO: &'static Info = &Info { name: "f32", layout: Layout::new::<f32>(), kind: Kind::F32 };97}98 99impl Reflect for u32 {100    const INFO: &'static Info = &Info { name: "u32", layout: Layout::new::<u32>(), kind: Kind::U32 };101}102 103impl Reflect for i32 {104    const INFO: &'static Info = &Info { name: "i32", layout: Layout::new::<i32>(), kind: Kind::I32 };105}106 107impl<const N: usize> Reflect for [u8; N] {108    const INFO: &'static Info = &Info { name: "text", layout: Layout::new::<[u8; N]>(), kind: Kind::Text };109}110 111macro_rules! is_hidden {112    () => {113        false114    };115    (hidden) => {116        true117    };118}119pub(crate) use is_hidden;120 121// Declares a plain-data struct and its reflect record. Two checks run at122// compile time: every field is Pod, and the struct is exactly as big as its123// fields, so it has no padding. A field written `#[hidden] timer: f32` is124// recorded as hidden.125macro_rules! pod {126    ($name:ident { $($(#[$attr:ident])? $field:ident: $ty:ty),* $(,)? }) => {127        #[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, Debug)]128        #[repr(C)]129        struct $name {130            $($field: $ty),*131        }132 133        const _: () = {134            use $crate::kayan::{Field, Info, Kind, Pod, Reflect};135 136            #[allow(unsafe_code)]137            unsafe impl Pod for $name {}138 139            impl Reflect for $name {140                const INFO: &'static Info = &Info {141                    name: stringify!($name),142                    layout: std::alloc::Layout::new::<$name>(),143                    kind: Kind::Struct(&[$(Field {144                        name: stringify!($field),145                        offset: std::mem::offset_of!($name, $field),146                        info: <$ty as Reflect>::INFO,147                        hidden: $crate::kayan::is_hidden!($($attr)?),148                    }),*]),149                };150            }151 152            const fn field_is_pod<T: Pod>() {}153            $(field_is_pod::<$ty>();)*154            assert!(size_of::<$name>() == 0 $(+ size_of::<$ty>())*, "a component has padding");155        };156    };157}158pub(crate) use pod;159 160// A plain-data enum: an i32 with named values. A Rust enum cannot be stored161// as bytes, because only its members are valid values and a column holds162// whatever bytes it holds. So the field is the number, and the record keeps163// the names, for tools. Only lesson 5 uses it.164#[allow(unused_macros)]165macro_rules! pod_enum {166    ($name:ident { $($member:ident = $value:literal),* $(,)? }) => {167        #[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]168        #[repr(transparent)]169        struct $name(i32);170 171        // A program need not name every member.172        #[allow(dead_code)]173        impl $name {174            $(const $member: $name = $name($value);)*175        }176 177        const _: () = {178            use $crate::kayan::{Info, Kind, Pod, Reflect};179 180            #[allow(unsafe_code)]181            unsafe impl Pod for $name {}182 183            impl Reflect for $name {184                const INFO: &'static Info = &Info {185                    name: stringify!($name),186                    layout: std::alloc::Layout::new::<$name>(),187                    kind: Kind::Enum(&[$((stringify!($member), $value)),*]),188                };189            }190        };191    };192}193#[allow(unused_imports)]194pub(crate) use pod_enum;195 196// A component: plain data with a record, and an id.197pub trait Component: Pod + Reflect {198    const ID: u32;199}200 201// pod!, plus the id: the ComponentId member with the same name as the struct.202macro_rules! component {203    ($name:ident { $($(#[$attr:ident])? $field:ident: $ty:ty),* $(,)? }) => {204        $crate::kayan::pod!($name { $($(#[$attr])? $field: $ty),* });205 206        impl $crate::kayan::Component for $name {207            const ID: u32 = ComponentId::$name as u32;208        }209    };210}211pub(crate) use component;212 213// One bit per component. A signature is a u64, so a world has at most 64.214pub fn bit(id: u32) -> u64 {215    1 << id216}217 218pub fn mask_of<T: Component>() -> u64 {219    bit(T::ID)220}221 222// A plain-data value as its bytes, for storing it somewhere that only knows223// bytes, like lesson 6's command buffer.224#[allow(unsafe_code)]225pub fn bytes_of<T: Pod>(value: &T) -> &[u8] {226    // SAFETY: T is Pod, so it has no padding and all its bytes are227    // initialised; the slice borrows `value` and cannot outlive it.228    unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts((value as *const T).cast::<u8>(), size_of::<T>()) }229}230 231// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------232// Entities233// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------234 235// A handle. `index` picks a slot in the world's slot list and `generation`236// says which life of that slot the handle was made for. Despawning bumps the237// slot's generation, so every handle to the dead entity stops matching, even238// after the index is reused. Generations start at 1, so "no entity" is None,239// and an Option<Entity> is no bigger than an Entity.240#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]241pub struct Entity {242    pub index: u32,243    pub generation: NonZeroU32,244}245 246impl fmt::Display for Entity {247    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {248        write!(f, "{}:{}", self.index, self.generation)249    }250}251 252const ONE: NonZeroU32 = NonZeroU32::MIN;253 254// Where an entity lives now: which table, which row. Rows move (swap-remove,255// lesson 2), so this is updated whenever one does. Handles never move. A free256// slot already holds its next generation, which no handle has yet, so the257// generation check alone says whether a handle is alive.258#[derive(Clone, Copy)]259pub struct Slot {260    pub generation: NonZeroU32,261    pub table: u32,262    pub row: u32,263}264 265// Why a structural change changed nothing: the handle no longer names a live266// entity. It is the only way one can fail.267#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]268pub struct Dead;269 270// "ok" or "dead", for printing what a change returned.271pub fn status(r: Result<(), Dead>) -> &'static str {272    match r {273        Ok(()) => "ok",274        Err(Dead) => "dead",275    }276}277 278// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------279// Columns: one component's rows, as bytes280// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------281 282// The storage of a column: 16-byte blocks, so it is aligned for any component283// a column accepts.284#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]285#[repr(C, align(16))]286struct Block([u8; 16]);287 288pub struct Column {289    blocks: Vec<Block>,290    pub info: &'static Info,291    id: u32,292}293 294impl Column {295    fn new(id: u32, info: &'static Info) -> Column {296        assert!(info.layout.align() <= 16, "{} needs more alignment than a column has", info.name);297        Column { blocks: Vec::new(), info, id }298    }299 300    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {301        self.info.layout.size()302    }303 304    #[allow(unsafe_code)]305    fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {306        // SAFETY: a Block is 16 initialised bytes with no padding, so the Vec's307        // buffer is `len * 16` initialised bytes.308        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(self.blocks.as_ptr().cast::<u8>(), self.blocks.len() * 16) }309    }310 311    #[allow(unsafe_code)]312    fn bytes_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [u8] {313        // SAFETY: as in bytes(); `&mut self` makes the view the only one.314        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(self.blocks.as_mut_ptr().cast::<u8>(), self.blocks.len() * 16) }315    }316 317    fn row(&self, row: usize) -> &[u8] {318        let size = self.size();319        &self.bytes()[row * size..(row + 1) * size]320    }321 322    fn row_mut(&mut self, row: usize) -> &mut [u8] {323        let size = self.size();324        &mut self.bytes_mut()[row * size..(row + 1) * size]325    }326 327    // Room for `capacity` rows. The rows move to the new allocation and the328    // old one is freed.329    fn grow(&mut self, capacity: usize) {330        self.blocks.resize((capacity * self.size()).div_ceil(16), Block::default());331    }332 333    fn copy_row(&mut self, to: usize, from: usize) {334        let size = self.size();335        self.bytes_mut().copy_within(from * size..(from + 1) * size, to * size);336    }337 338    fn zero_row(&mut self, row: usize) {339        self.row_mut(row).fill(0);340    }341 342    #[allow(unsafe_code)]343    fn slice<T: Component>(&self, count: usize) -> &[T] {344        assert!(self.id == T::ID, "a {} column read as {}", self.info.name, T::INFO.name);345        let bytes = &self.bytes()[..count * size_of::<T>()];346        // SAFETY: T is the column's component, so the bytes are `count` T's;347        // the storage is aligned to 16 and T needs at most 16; T is Pod, so348        // any bytes are a valid T.349        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(bytes.as_ptr().cast::<T>(), count) }350    }351 352    #[allow(unsafe_code)]353    fn slice_mut<T: Component>(&mut self, count: usize) -> &mut [T] {354        assert!(self.id == T::ID, "a {} column read as {}", self.info.name, T::INFO.name);355        let bytes = &mut self.bytes_mut()[..count * size_of::<T>()];356        // SAFETY: as in slice(). T has no padding, so writing a T leaves every357        // byte initialised, and the byte views stay valid.358        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(bytes.as_mut_ptr().cast::<T>(), count) }359    }360}361 362// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------363// Tables364// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------365 366// One archetype. `entities[row]` is the handle of the entity in that row,367// which is how a swap-remove finds the slot to fix. `columns[id]` is Some when368// the signature has bit `id`. The row count is the length of `entities`.369pub struct Table {370    pub signature: u64,371    pub capacity: usize,372    pub entities: Vec<Entity>,373    pub columns: [Option<Column>; 64],374}375 376// The tables a system wants: every component in `all`, none in `none`.377#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]378pub struct Query {379    pub all: u64,380    pub none: u64,381}382 383impl Table {384    // A table for a signature: one empty column per component in it.385    fn new(infos: &[Option<&'static Info>; 64], signature: u64) -> Table {386        let mut columns = [const { None }; 64];387        for id in 0..64 {388            if signature & bit(id) != 0 {389                let info = infos[id as usize]390                    .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("signature {signature} uses component {id}, which was never registered"));391                columns[id as usize] = Some(Column::new(id, info));392            }393        }394        Table { signature, capacity: 0, entities: Vec::new(), columns }395    }396 397    pub fn count(&self) -> usize {398        self.entities.len()399    }400 401    pub fn has(&self, id: u32) -> bool {402        self.signature & bit(id) != 0403    }404 405    pub fn matches(&self, q: Query) -> bool {406        (self.signature & q.all) == q.all && (self.signature & q.none) == 0407    }408 409    // Room for 16 rows at first, then double, in `entities` and every column.410    fn grow(&mut self) {411        self.capacity = if self.capacity == 0 { 16 } else { self.capacity * 2 };412        self.entities.reserve_exact(self.capacity - self.entities.len());413        for c in self.columns.iter_mut().flatten() {414            c.grow(self.capacity);415        }416    }417 418    // A new row with zeroed components, owned by `e`.419    fn add_row(&mut self, e: Entity) -> usize {420        if self.count() == self.capacity {421            self.grow();422        }423        let row = self.count();424        self.entities.push(e);425        for c in self.columns.iter_mut().flatten() {426            c.zero_row(row);427        }428        row429    }430 431    // Swap-remove: the last row moves into `row`, and the slot of the entity432    // that moved is told its new row. This is the line lesson 2 could not433    // write. The slots are the world's, so the world passes them in.434    fn remove_row(&mut self, row: usize, slots: &mut [Slot]) {435        let last = self.count() - 1;436        if row != last {437            for c in self.columns.iter_mut().flatten() {438                c.copy_row(row, last);439            }440        }441        self.entities.swap_remove(row);442        if let Some(moved) = self.entities.get(row) {443            slots[moved.index as usize].row = row as u32;444        }445    }446 447    // T's column, cut to the rows in use. Asking for a column the table does448    // not have is a bug in the caller, so it stops the program.449    pub fn column<T: Component>(&self) -> &[T] {450        self.columns[T::ID as usize]451            .as_ref()452            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("table {} has no {} column", self.signature, T::INFO.name))453            .slice::<T>(self.count())454    }455 456    pub fn column_mut<T: Component>(&mut self) -> &mut [T] {457        let count = self.count();458        self.columns[T::ID as usize]459            .as_mut()460            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("table {} has no {} column", self.signature, T::INFO.name))461            .slice_mut::<T>(count)462    }463 464    // Two columns at once, the first to write. They must be two different465    // components, which is checked when the program is built.466    pub fn pair_mut<A: Component, B: Component>(&mut self) -> (&mut [A], &[B]) {467        const { assert!(A::ID != B::ID, "pair_mut needs two different components") };468        let (count, signature) = (self.count(), self.signature);469        let [a, b] = self.columns.get_disjoint_mut([A::ID as usize, B::ID as usize]).expect("two different columns");470        let a = a.as_mut().unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("table {signature} has no {} column", A::INFO.name));471        let b = b.as_ref().unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("table {signature} has no {} column", B::INFO.name));472        (a.slice_mut::<A>(count), b.slice::<B>(count))473    }474}475 476// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------477// The world478// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------479 480// The registry, every table, and the entity index. Tables are referred to by481// index: making a table can grow `tables` and move all of them, and an index482// survives that.483pub struct World {484    pub infos: [Option<&'static Info>; 64],485    pub component_count: u32,486    pub tables: Vec<Table>,487    pub by_signature: HashMap<u64, u32>,488    pub slots: Vec<Slot>,489    pub free: Vec<u32>,490    pub live: usize,491}492 493impl World {494    pub fn new() -> World {495        World {496            infos: [None; 64],497            component_count: 0,498            tables: Vec::new(),499            by_signature: HashMap::new(),500            slots: Vec::new(),501            free: Vec::new(),502            live: 0,503        }504    }505 506    pub fn register<T: Component>(&mut self) {507        assert!(T::ID < 64, "component id {} is past the 64 a signature can hold", T::ID);508        self.infos[T::ID as usize] = Some(T::INFO);509        self.component_count = self.component_count.max(T::ID + 1);510    }511 512    pub fn info(&self, id: u32) -> &'static Info {513        self.infos[id as usize].expect("every component in a signature is registered")514    }515 516    // The table for a signature, made the first time anything needs it.517    pub fn table_for(&mut self, signature: u64) -> u32 {518        if let Some(&index) = self.by_signature.get(&signature) {519            return index;520        }521        let index = self.tables.len() as u32;522        self.tables.push(Table::new(&self.infos, signature));523        self.by_signature.insert(signature, index);524        index525    }526 527    pub fn alive(&self, e: Entity) -> bool {528        self.slots.get(e.index as usize).is_some_and(|s| s.generation == e.generation)529    }530 531    // A new entity with the components in `signature`, all zeroed. A freed532    // index is reused before a new one is made, with the generation its533    // despawn left behind.534    pub fn spawn(&mut self, signature: u64) -> Entity {535        let index = match self.free.pop() {536            Some(index) => index,537            None => {538                self.slots.push(Slot { generation: ONE, table: 0, row: 0 });539                self.slots.len() as u32 - 1540            }541        };542        let e = Entity { index, generation: self.slots[index as usize].generation };543        let table = self.table_for(signature);544        let row = self.tables[table as usize].add_row(e);545        self.slots[index as usize] = Slot { generation: e.generation, table, row: row as u32 };546        self.live += 1;547        e548    }549 550    // A dead handle changes nothing, so despawning twice is harmless.551    pub fn despawn(&mut self, e: Entity) -> Result<(), Dead> {552        if !self.alive(e) {553            return Err(Dead);554        }555        let Slot { table, row, .. } = self.slots[e.index as usize];556        self.tables[table as usize].remove_row(row as usize, &mut self.slots);557        let slot = &mut self.slots[e.index as usize];558        slot.generation = slot.generation.checked_add(1).expect("a slot has lived 4 billion lives");559        self.free.push(e.index);560        self.live -= 1;561        Ok(())562    }563 564    // The components a live entity has: its table's signature. 0 for a dead565    // one.566    pub fn signature(&self, e: Entity) -> u64 {567        if !self.alive(e) {568            return 0;569        }570        self.tables[self.slots[e.index as usize].table as usize].signature571    }572 573    // Move `e` to the table for `signature`. Components both tables have are574    // copied; components only the new table has start zeroed; components only575    // the old table has are dropped.576    pub fn move_to(&mut self, e: Entity, signature: u64) -> Result<(), Dead> {577        if !self.alive(e) {578            return Err(Dead);579        }580        let Slot { table: from, row, .. } = self.slots[e.index as usize];581        if self.tables[from as usize].signature == signature {582            return Ok(());583        }584        // table_for can make a table and move them all, so no table is585        // borrowed until it returns.586        let to = self.table_for(signature);587        let [old, new] = self.tables.get_disjoint_mut([from as usize, to as usize]).expect("two different tables");588        let new_row = new.add_row(e);589        for (o, n) in old.columns.iter().zip(new.columns.iter_mut()) {590            if let (Some(o), Some(n)) = (o, n) {591                n.row_mut(new_row).copy_from_slice(o.row(row as usize));592            }593        }594        old.remove_row(row as usize, &mut self.slots);595        self.slots[e.index as usize] = Slot { generation: e.generation, table: to, row: new_row as u32 };596        Ok(())597    }598 599    // e's T, or None if e is dead or has no T.600    pub fn get<T: Component>(&self, e: Entity) -> Option<&T> {601        if !self.alive(e) {602            return None;603        }604        let Slot { table, row, .. } = self.slots[e.index as usize];605        let t = &self.tables[table as usize];606        t.has(T::ID).then(|| &t.column::<T>()[row as usize])607    }608 609    pub fn get_mut<T: Component>(&mut self, e: Entity) -> Option<&mut T> {610        if !self.alive(e) {611            return None;612        }613        let Slot { table, row, .. } = self.slots[e.index as usize];614        let t = &mut self.tables[table as usize];615        t.has(T::ID).then(|| &mut t.column_mut::<T>()[row as usize])616    }617 618    // e's component `id` as its bytes, or None if e is dead or has no such619    // component. For tools that work from reflect records rather than from620    // types, like lesson 5's inspector.621    pub fn get_bytes(&self, e: Entity, id: u32) -> Option<&[u8]> {622        if !self.alive(e) || id >= self.component_count {623            return None;624        }625        let Slot { table, row, .. } = self.slots[e.index as usize];626        self.tables[table as usize].columns[id as usize].as_ref().map(|c| c.row(row as usize))627    }628 629    pub fn get_bytes_mut(&mut self, e: Entity, id: u32) -> Option<&mut [u8]> {630        if !self.alive(e) || id >= self.component_count {631            return None;632        }633        let Slot { table, row, .. } = self.slots[e.index as usize];634        self.tables[table as usize].columns[id as usize].as_mut().map(|c| c.row_mut(row as usize))635    }636 637    // Give e a T, moving it to a new table if it did not have one.638    pub fn add<T: Component>(&mut self, e: Entity, value: T) -> Result<(), Dead> {639        self.move_to(e, self.signature(e) | mask_of::<T>())?;640        *self.get_mut::<T>(e).expect("its table has a T now") = value;641        Ok(())642    }643 644    // Take e's T away, moving it to the table without it.645    pub fn remove<T: Component>(&mut self, e: Entity) -> Result<(), Dead> {646        self.move_to(e, self.signature(e) & !mask_of::<T>())647    }648 649    // Every row of every table must belong to a live entity whose slot points650    // back at that table and row, and the rows must add up to the live count.651    // Returns how many of those checks failed, printing each.652    pub fn verify(&self) -> usize {653        let mut problems = 0;654        let mut rows = 0;655        for (ti, t) in self.tables.iter().enumerate() {656            for (row, &e) in t.entities.iter().enumerate() {657                if !self.alive(e) {658                    println!("verify: table {ti} row {row} holds dead entity {e}");659                    problems += 1;660                    continue;661                }662                let s = self.slots[e.index as usize];663                if s.table as usize != ti || s.row as usize != row {664                    println!("verify: {e} is in table {ti} row {row}, its slot says table {} row {}", s.table, s.row);665                    problems += 1;666                }667            }668            rows += t.count();669        }670        if rows != self.live {671            println!("verify: {rows} rows in tables, {} entities alive", self.live);672            problems += 1;673        }674        problems675    }676 677    // A signature as names, {Position Velocity}.678    pub fn names(&self, signature: u64) -> String {679        let names: Vec<&str> = (0..self.component_count)680            .filter(|&id| signature & bit(id) != 0)681            .map(|id| self.info(id).name)682            .collect();683        format!("{{{}}}", names.join(" "))684    }685 686    pub fn print_tables(&self) {687        for (ti, t) in self.tables.iter().enumerate() {688            print!("    table {ti} {}:", self.names(t.signature));689            for e in &t.entities {690                print!(" {e}");691            }692            println!();693        }694    }695}

Tooling

Build and check

tools/check.py runs every program and diffs its output

1"""Build every program, run it, and compare what it prints with its .expected file.2 3    python tools/check.py               every program, Debug4    python tools/check.py archetype     only programs whose path contains "archetype"5    python tools/check.py --release     optimised, without debug assertions6    python tools/check.py --bless       rewrite the .expected files from this run7    python tools/check.py --clippy      also run cargo clippy over everything8    python tools/check.py --miri        run the programs that use `unsafe` under Miri9 10The dojo's blocks are checked too (`python tools/check.py dojo` for only them):11each block's harness is built with its reference solution and must print its12harness.expected; level 1 must build and fail, since it has a gap; level 213must build. The playgrounds are [[bin]]s, so they are checked like the rest.14 15A program passes only if every step is clean:16 17  1. rustc reports no warnings (-D warnings),18  2. the program exits with 0,19  3. its output matches the .expected file beside it, byte for byte.20 21Every program is a single file built with plain `rustc`, the way you would22build it by hand. The programs are the [[bin]] list in Cargo.toml, so there is23one list to keep, and `cargo build` builds the same files.24 25rustc is RUSTC or `rustc` on PATH. Miri needs a nightly toolchain with the miri26component (`rustup toolchain install nightly --component miri`).27"""28 29from __future__ import annotations30 31import os32import re33import compare(actual: str, expected_path: Path, bless: bool) -> tuple[bool, str]:56    actual = actual.replace("\r\n", "\n")57    if bless:58        expected_path.write_text(actual, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")59        return True, "blessed"60    if not expected_path.exists():61        return False, f"no {expected_path.name}; run with --bless after reading the output:\n{actual}"62    expected = expected_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n")63    if actual != expected:64        got, want = actual.splitlines(), expected.splitlines()65        for i in range(max(len(got), len(want))):66            g = got[i] if i < len(got) else "<missing>"67            w = want[i] if i < len(want) else "<missing>"68            if g != w:69                return False, f"line {i + 1}\n  got:  {g}\n  want: {w}"70    return True, ""71 72 73def check(rustc: str, name: str, source: Path, release: bool, bless: bool) -> tuple[bool, str]:74    work = OUT / ("release" if release else "debug")75    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)76    exe = work / (f"{name}.exe" if os.name == "nt" else name)77    flags = ["--edition", "2024", "-g", "-D", "warnings", "--crate-name", name]78    if release:79        flags += ["-C", "opt-level=3", "-C", "debug-assertions=off"]80    build = run([rustc, *flags, str(source), "-o", str(exe)])81    if build.returncode != 0 or build.stdout.strip():82        return False, "rustc:\n" + build.stdout83    ran = run([str(exe)])84    if ran.returncode != 0:85        return False, f"exit {ran.returncode}:\n{ran.stdout}"86    return compare(ran.stdout, source.with_suffix(".expected"), bless)87 88 89def with_modules(source: Path) -> str:90    """A program's text, and the text of each module it includes by path."""91    text folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)122    shutil.copyfile(block / "harness.rs", folder / "harness.rs")123    shutil.copyfile(kata, folder / "kata.rs")124    # The harness says #[path = "harness.expected", bless)142    if not ok:143        return False, detail144    for level in (1, 2):145        exe, err = dojo_build(rustc, block, block / "levels" / f"{level}.rs", f"level{level}", run([str(exe)]).returncode == 0:150            return False, "level 1 passes the harness as given; its gap is not a gap"151    return True, detail152 153 154def clippy_dojo(rustc: str, block: Path) ->  f'[package]\nname = "dojo-check"\nversion = "0.1.0"\nedition = "2024"\nautobins = false\n\n'169        f'[[bin]]\nname = "harness"\npath = "{harness.as_posix()}"\n', encoding="utf-8")170    env = ran.stdout.splitlines():173        return False, f"miri, exit {ran.returncode}:\n{ran.stdout}"174    return True, ""175 176 177def main() -> int:178    args = sys.argv[1:]179    release = "--release" in args180    bless = "--bless" in args181    filters = [a for a in args if not a.startswith("--")]182 183    rustc = os.environ.get("RUSTC") or shutil.which("rustc")184    if not rustc:185        sys.exit("check: rustc not found; set RUSTC or put rustc on PATH")186    programs = [(n, p) for n, p in programs_from_cargo_toml()187                if not filters or any(f in p.as_posix() for f in print(f"{'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {rel}" + (f"  ({detail})" if ok and detail else ""))194        if not ok:195            failed += 1196            print("     " + detail.replace("\n", "\n     "))197    print(f"{len(programs) - failed} of {len(programs)} passed")198 199    blocks = [b for b in dojo_blocks()200              if not filters or any(f in b.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix() for f in print("     " + detail.replace("\n", "\n     "))209    if blocks:210        print(f"{len(blocks) - dojo_failed} of {len(blocks)} dojo blocks passed")211    failed += dojo_failed212 213    if clippy.stdout.strip() else "FAIL"))216        if clippy.returncode != 0 or clippy.stdout.strip():217            failed += 1218            print("     " + clippy.stdout.replace("\n", "\n     "))219 tools/check_snippets.py

1"""Check that the code and output samples in the guides match the programs they2come from.3 4    python tools/check_snippets.py5 6Each guide in ecs/docs and docs names its program's source on a line of its7own, in backticks; each dojo block's README is checked against every file of8its block. Then:9 10  * every ```rust block must appear in that source, or in a module it brings11    in with #[path], exactly, as consecutive lines, indentation included;12  * every plain ``` block whose first line is a line of the program's13    .expected is an output sample: its lines, except "...", must appear in the14    .expected in the same order.15 16Blocks fenced ```rust ignore are code that is not in the program on purpose,17usually because it does not compile, and are not checked; nor are ```rin18blocks, which quote the rin-dod version, or plain blocks that do not start19with an output line, such as diagrams and compiler errors. A guide that passes20can be copied from with confidence.21"""22 23from __future__ import annotations24 25import re26import sys27from pathlib import Path28 29ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent30DOCS = [ROOT / "ecs" / "docs", ROOT / "docs"]31 32 33def blocks(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], int]]:34    """(info string, lines, line number) for every fenced block."""35    found = []36    lines = text.split("\n")37    i = 038    while i < len(lines):39        m = re.match(r"^```([\w ,]*)\s*$", lines[i])40        if m:41            info, start, body = m.group(1).strip(), i + 1, []42            i += 143            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() != "```":44                body.append(lines[i])45                i += 146            found.append((info, body, start))47        i += 148    return found49 50 51def with_modules(source_path: Path) -> list[str]:52    """The program's text, and the text of each module it includes by path."""53    source = source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")54    texts = [source]55    for path in re.findall(r'^#\[path = "([^"]+)"\]', source, re.M):56        texts.append((source_path.parent / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))57    return texts58 59 60def in_order(sample: list[str], expected: list[str]) -> bool:61    at = 062    for line in sample:63        if line.strip() == "...":64            continue65        try:66            at = expected.index(line, at) + 167        except ValueError:68            return False69    return True70 71 72# A dojo block's README quotes its playground, its harness, the shared dojo.rs73# and the level files, so a sample may come from any of them, and an output74# sample from the playground's or the harness's expected output.75def dojo_sources(block: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[Path]]:76    files = sorted(block.rglob("*.rs")) + [block.parent / "dojo.rs"]77    texts = [f.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for f in files if f.name != "kata.rs" or f.parent.name == "solution"]78    outputs = sorted(block.glob("*.expected"))79    expected = [line for o in outputs if o.exists() for line in o.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n")]80    return texts, expected, outputs81 82 83def guides() -> list[tuple[Path, list[str], list[str], str, str]]:84    """(guide, source texts, expected lines, what the code is, what the output is)"""85    found = []86    for docs in DOCS:87        for doc in sorted(docs.glob("*.md")):88            m = re.search(r"^`((?:ecs/)?src/[^`]+\.rs)`", doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.M)89            if not m:90                continue91            source_path = ROOT / m.group(1)92            expected_path = source_path.with_suffix(".expected")93            expected = expected_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n") if expected_path.exists() else []94            found.append((doc, with_modules(source_path), expected, m.group(1),95                          expected_path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()))96    for block in sorted(p for p in (ROOT / "dojo").glob("*.*") if (p / "README.md").exists()):97        texts, expected, _ = dojo_sources(block)98        name = block.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()99        found.append((block / "README.md", texts, expected, name, name + "'s expected output"))100    return found101 102 103def main() -> int:104    failures = 0105    checked = 0106    for doc, sources, expected, code_name, output_name in guides():107        text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")108        for info, body, line in blocks(text):109            if info == "rust":110                checked += 1111                if not any("\n".join(body) in text for text in sources):112                    failures += 1113                    print(f"{doc.relative_to(ROOT)}:{line}: rust sample not found in {code_name}")114                    for b in body[:3]:115                        print(f"      {b}")116            elif info == "" and body and body[0] in expected:117                checked += 1118                if not in_order(body, expected):119                    failures += 1120                    print(f"{doc.relative_to(ROOT)}:{line}: output sample does not match {output_name}")121    print(f"{checked - failures} of {checked} samples match")122    return 1 if failures else 0123 124 125if __name__ == "__main__":126    sys.exit(main())

1"""The dojo's runner: start a kata, run it against its harness, keep your times.2 3    python tools/dojo.py                         the blocks, your reps, and what is due4    python tools/dojo.py start slot_map 2        a fresh kata.rs from level 2; the clock starts5    python tools/dojo.py slot_map                build the harness with your kata.rs and run it6    python tools/dojo.py slot_map --seed 42 --stop 13377                                                 the same fuzz run, stopping before operation 13378    python tools/dojo.py slot_map --release      optimised, for big --ops9    python tools/dojo.py slot_map --miri         under Miri, for katas with unsafe (nightly)10    python tools/dojo.py play slot_map           the block's playground11 12A block can be named by its number, its name, or the start of its name:13`3`, `slot_map` and `slot` are the same block.14 15When a started kata passes, the time since `start` is added to dojo/log.md,16and the block is due again after 1, 3, 7, 14, then 30 days, counting its17passes. Spaced reps are what make a block stick, more than many in one day.18 19Your kata.rs files are yours: git ignores them, and `start` will not20overwrite one you have changed unless you add --force.21"""22 23from __future__ import annotations24 25import datetime as dt26import json27import os28import re29import shutil30import subprocess31import sys32from pathlib import Path33 34ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent35DOJO = ROOT / "dojo"36OUT = ROOT / "build" / "dojo"37LOG = DOJO / "log.md"38STARTED = DOJO / ".started.json"39INTERVALS = [1, 3, 7, 14, 30]40 41 42def blocks() -> list[Path]:43    return sorted(p for p in DOJO.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and re.match(r"\d+\.", p.name))44 45 46def name_of(block: Path) -> str:47    return block.name.split(".", 1)[1]48 49 50def find(word: str) -> Path:51    found = [b for b in blocks() if word in (b.name, name_of(b), b.name.split(".")[0])]52    found = found or [b for b in blocks() if name_of(b).startswith(word)]53    if len(found) != 1:54        sys.exit(f"dojo: no single block called {word!r}; the blocks are "55                 + ", ".join(name_of(b) for b in blocks()))56    return found[0]57 58 59# The target times, from the level table in each block's README:60# | 2 | every function | 8:00 |61def targets(block: Path) -> dict[int, str]:62    readme = block / "README.md"63    text = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if readme.exists() else ""64    return {int(m.group(1)): m.group(2) for m in re.finditer(r"^\| (\d) \|.*\| (\d+:\d\d) \|$", text, re.M)}65 66 67def run(cmd: list[str], cwd: Path = ROOT, env: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> int:68    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, env=env).returncode69 70 71def rustc() -> str:72    found = os.environ.get("RUSTC") or shutil.which("rustc")73    if not found:74        sys.exit("dojo: rustc not found; set RUSTC or put rustc on PATH")75    return found76 77 78# A kata in progress is full of unused arguments and fields, so the warnings79# for those are off; tools/check.py builds the solutions with every warning80# as an error.81def build(source: Path, exe: Path, release: bool) -> None:82    exe.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)83    flags = ["--edition", "2024", "-g", "-A", "unused"]84    if release:85        flags += ["-C", "opt-level=3", "-C", "debug-assertions=off"]86    if run([rustc(), *flags, str(source), "-o", str(exe)]) != 0:87        sys.exit(1)88 89 90def load_started() -> dict:91    try:92        return json.loads(STARTED.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))93    except (OSError, ValueError):94        return {}95 96 97def save_started(started: dict) -> None:98    STARTED.write_text(json.dumps(started, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")99 100 101def log_rows() -> list[list[str]]:102    if not LOG.exists():103        return []104    rows = []105    for line in LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():106        cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]107        if len(cells) == 4 and re.match(r"\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d", cells[0]):108            rows.append(cells)109    return rows110 111 112def minutes(seconds: float) -> str:113    s = int(round(seconds))114    return f"{s // 60}:{s % 60:02d}"115 116 117def seconds(text: str) -> int:118    m, s = text.split(":")119    return int(m) * 60 + int(s)120 121 122def due(passes: list[dt.date]) -> dt.date | None:123    if not passes:124        return None125    return max(passes) + dt.timedelta(days=INTERVALS[min(len(passes), len(INTERVALS)) - 1])126 127 128def status() -> int:129    rows = log_rows()130    today = dt.date.today()131    started = load_started()132    print(f"{'block':<16}{'reps':>5}  {'best time, level':<18}{'last':<12}next")133    for b in blocks():134        mine = [r for r in rows if r[1] == name_of(b)]135        passes = [dt.date.fromisoformat(r[0]) for r in mine]136        best = min(mine, key=lambda r: (-int(r[2]), seconds(r[3])), default=None)137        best_text = f"{best[3]}, level {best[2]}" if best else "-"138        next_day = due(passes)139        next_text = "now" if next_day is None or next_day <= today else next_day.isoformat()140        if name_of(b) in started:141            next_text = f"started, level {started[name_of(b)]['level']}"142        last = max(passes).isoformat() if passes else "-"143        print(f"{b.name:<16}{len(mine):>5}  {best_text:<18}{last:<12}{next_text}")144    print()145    print("start one with: python tools/dojo.py start <block> <level 1 to 3>")146    return 0147 148 149def start(word: str, level: str, force: bool) -> int:150    b = find(word)151    source = b / "levels" / f"{level}.rs"152    if not source.exists():153        sys.exit(f"dojo: {name_of(b)} has no level {level}; the levels are "154                 + ", ".join(p.stem for p in sorted((b / "levels").glob("*.rs"))))155    kata = b / "kata.rs"156    untouched = [p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in (b / "levels").glob("*.rs")]157    if kata.exists() and kata.read_text(encoding="utf-8") not in untouched and not force:158        sys.exit(f"dojo: {kata.relative_to(ROOT)} has your work in it; add --force to replace it")159    shutil.copyfile(source, kata)160    started = load_started()161    started[name_of(b)] = {"level": int(level), "at": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}162    save_started(started)163    target = targets(b).get(int(level))164    print(f"{kata.relative_to(ROOT)} is level {level}" + (f"; the target is {target}" if target else ""))165    print(f"the clock is running. Test it with: python tools/dojo.py {name_of(b)}")166    return 0167 168 169def check(word: str, args: list[str]) -> int:170    b = find(word)171    if not (b / "kata.rs").exists():172        sys.exit(f"dojo: no kata.rs in {b.relative_to(ROOT)} yet; start one with: "173                 f"python tools/dojo.py start {name_of(b)} 1")174    release = "--release" in args175    passthrough = [a for a in args if a not in ("--release", "--miri")]176    if "--miri" in args:177        code, out = miri(b, passthrough)178    else:179        exe = OUT / name_of(b) / ("harness.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "harness")180        build(b / "harness.rs", exe, release)181        code, out = stream([str(exe), *passthrough])182    if code != 0 or "PASS" not in out.splitlines():183        return 1184    started = load_started()185    entry = started.pop(name_of(b), None)186    if entry and not passthrough:187        took = (dt.datetime.now() - dt.datetime.fromisoformat(entry["at"])).total_seconds()188        if not LOG.exists():189            LOG.write_text("# Dojo log\n\n| date | block | level | time |\n|---|---|---|---|\n", encoding="utf-8")190        with LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:191            f.write(f"| {dt.date.today().isoformat()} | {name_of(b)} | {entry['level']} | {minutes(took)} |\n")192        save_started(started)193        target = targets(b).get(entry["level"])194        print(f"\nlevel {entry['level']} in {minutes(took)}" + (f", target {target}" if target else ""))195        passes = [dt.date.fromisoformat(r[0]) for r in log_rows() if r[1] == name_of(b)]196        print(f"logged in {LOG.relative_to(ROOT)}; {name_of(b)} is due again on {due(passes).isoformat()}")197    return 0198 199 200# Miri runs through cargo, so the harness gets a small package of its own,201# pointing at the files where they are.202def miri(b: Path, args: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str]:203    pkg = OUT / name_of(b) / "miri"204    pkg.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)205    (pkg / "Cargo.toml").write_text(206        f'[package]\nname = "dojo-{name_of(b).replace("_", "-")}"\nversion = "0.1.0"\nedition = "2024"\n'207        f'autobins = false\n\n[[bin]]\nname = "harness"\npath = "{(b / "harness.rs").as_posix()}"\n',208        encoding="utf-8")209    if "--ops" not in args:210        args = args + ["--ops", "500"]211    env = dict(os.environ, MIRIFLAGS="-Zmiri-strict-provenance")212    return stream(["cargo", "+nightly", "miri", "run", "-q", "--", *args], cwd=pkg, env=env)213 214 215# Run a program, printing what it prints as it prints it, panics included, and216# keep the text to look for PASS in.217def stream(cmd: list[str], cwd: Path = ROOT, env: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> tuple[int, str]:218    lines = []219    with subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=cwd, env=env, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,220                          stderr=subprocess.STDOUT) as p:221        for line in p.stdout:222            print(line, end="", flush=True)223            lines.append(line)224    return p.returncode, "".join(lines)225 226 227def play(word: str) -> int:228    b = find(word)229    exe = OUT / name_of(b) / ("playground.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "playground")230    build(b / f"play_{name_of(b)}.rs", exe, False)231    return run([str(exe)])232 233 234def main() -> int:235    args = sys.argv[1:]236    if not args:237        return status()238    if args[0] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):239        print(__doc__)240        return 0241    if args[0] == "start":242        rest = [a for a in args[1:] if a != "--force"]243        if len(rest) != 2:244            sys.exit("dojo: start <block> <level>")245        return start(rest[0], rest[1], "--force" in args)246    if args[0] == "play":247        if len(args) != 2:248            sys.exit("dojo: play <block>")249        return play(args[1])250    return check(args[0], args[1:])251 252 253if __name__ == "__main__":254    sys.exit(main())

1// What every harness in the dojo shares: the run's settings, a random number2// generator that gives the same numbers everywhere, how a step is checked, and3// how a failure is reported. It also holds the two types the katas take as4// given: a Handle, and Dead.5//6// A harness brings it in the way lessons 4 to 6 bring in kayan:7//8//   #[path = "../dojo.rs"]9//   mod dojo;10 11// Not every harness uses every part.12#![allow(dead_code)]13 14use std::fmt;15use std::num::NonZeroU32;16use std::process::exit;17use std::sync::Mutex;18 19// Where the run is: the last scenario step that passed, or the fuzz operation20// running now. A panic in the kata reports it, since the panic itself only21// knows the line it happened on.22static WHERE: Mutex<String> = Mutex::new(String::new());23 24fn now_at(text: String) {25    if let Ok(mut at) = WHERE.lock() {26        *at = text;27    }28}29 30// A generational handle: an index, and which life of that index it was made31// for. Generations start at 1, so an Option<Handle> costs nothing extra.32#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]33pub struct Handle {34    pub index: u32,35    pub generation: NonZeroU32,36}37 38impl fmt::Display for Handle {39    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {40        write!(f, "{}:{}", self.index, self.generation)41    }42}43 44// Why a change changed nothing: the handle no longer names anything alive.45#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]46pub struct Dead;47 48// One harness run: which block, the fuzz seed, how many operations, and where49// to stop for the debugger. The command line sets them:50//51//   harness --seed 42 --ops 5000 --stop 133752pub struct Run {53    block: &'static str,54    pub seed: u64,55    pub ops: u64,56    stop: Option<u64>,57}58 59impl Run {60    pub fn new(block: &'static str, title: &str) -> Run {61        let mut run = Run { block, seed: 1, ops: 20000, stop: None };62        let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();63        for pair in args.chunks(2) {64            let value = pair.get(1).and_then(|v| v.parse().ok());65            match (pair[0].as_str(), value) {66                ("--seed", Some(v)) => run.seed = v,67                ("--ops", Some(v)) => run.ops = v,68                ("--stop", Some(v)) => run.stop = Some(v),69                _ => {70                    println!("usage: harness [--seed N] [--ops N] [--stop N]");71                    exit(2);72                }73            }74        }75        println!("dojo: {title}");76        now_at("FAIL in the scenario: it panicked before the first step passed".to_string());77        std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(|info| {78            let at = WHERE.lock().map(|at| at.clone()).unwrap_or_default();79            println!("{at}");80            println!("    {info}");81        }));82        run83    }84 85    // A step of the scenario: what was done, what came back, and what should86    // have. Printed when it matches; the end of the run when it does not.87    pub fn same(&self, what: &str, got: impl fmt::Display, want: &str) {88        let got = got.to_string();89        if got != want {90            println!("FAIL in the scenario: {what} gave {got}, it should give {want}");91            exit(1);92        }93        println!("    {what}: {got}");94        now_at(format!("FAIL in the scenario: it panicked after \"{what}\" passed"));95    }96 97    pub fn fuzz(&self) {98        println!("fuzz: {} operations from seed {}, checked after each", self.ops, self.seed);99        now_at("FAIL in the fuzz run: it panicked before the first operation".to_string());100    }101 102    // Call before operation `op`. With --stop at this operation, it says what103    // is about to run and calls stop_here, so a breakpoint there lands just104    // before the operation that fails.105    pub fn before(&self, op: u64, what: impl fmt::Display) {106        now_at(format!(107            "FAIL at operation {op} (seed {}): it panicked, in {what}\n    debug it: build/dojo/{}/harness --seed {} --stop {op}",108            self.seed, self.block, self.seed109        ));110        if self.stop == Some(op) {111            println!("stopped before operation {op}: {what}");112            stop_here(op);113        }114    }115 116    // A check during the fuzz run. The message says what went wrong; the117    // second line says how to get back here in the debugger.118    pub fn check(&self, op: u64, holds: bool, what: impl FnOnce() -> String) {119        if !holds {120            println!("FAIL at operation {op} (seed {}): {}", self.seed, what());121            println!("    debug it: build/dojo/{}/harness --seed {} --stop {op}", self.block, self.seed);122            println!("    with a breakpoint on stop_here, which runs just before that operation");123            exit(1);124        }125    }126 127    pub fn pass(&self) {128        println!("PASS");129    }130}131 132// Set a breakpoint here, and run with --stop N.133#[inline(never)]134pub fn stop_here(op: u64) {135    std::hint::black_box(op);136}137 138// splitmix64: a few lines, fast, and the same numbers on every machine and in139// rin-dod's dojo, so a seed means the same run everywhere.140pub struct Rng(u64);141 142impl Rng {143    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Rng {144        Rng(seed)145    }146 147    pub fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {148        self.0 = self.0.wrapping_add(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15);149        let mut z = self.0;150        z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9);151        z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D049BB133111EB);152        z ^ (z >> 31)153    }154 155    // A number in 0..n.156    pub fn below(&mut self, n: u64) -> u64 {157        self.next() % n158    }159 160    // One of `items`, at random.161    pub fn pick<T: Copy>(&mut self, items: &[T]) -> T {162        items[self.below(items.len() as u64) as usize]163    }164}
